notes.title: Patch #7
notes.notes:
Hey, Crewmates!  We hope you're still enjoying conquering the Wasteland - thank you so much for the support so far!   We're dropping by with a slightly larger patch this time. Let us help you get settled in as we explain the newly implemented Quality of Life improvements, driving options and difficulty settings.


PATCH NOTES
 Added options to turn off the driver’s ability to automatically avoid obstacles and follow roads. This was following feedback from players that the driver's AI would sometimes behave in an undesirable way around certain environmental objects. With these options, players can now switch to more manual control over the Battle Wagon’s movement.


 Added a QoL improvement to the Crew Facility Upgrades. Previously the upgrades would simply increase the maximum level that recruitable crew members would appear at in the Citadel. The skill points of those recruited members until that point would already be pre-assigned meaning that players would have a hard time acquiring recruits who they wanted to specialize in certain skills (especially towards the end-game). Now when you upgrade the crew facilities – any skill points the crew member would have acquired up until that point will be available to assign to any skill the player wishes (rather than already being distributed). We hope with this change this gives players more freedom to customise their perfect crew!


 Additional text prompts to aid with controller support. This was following feedback where players were struggling to use a controller in certain parts of the game. We’ve now added additional prompts so it’s clearer for players.


 Added 2 new difficulty options: ‘Hard’ and Hardest'. As requested by many players - we’ve now added harder difficulty modes! (You can change this whenever you return to the Citadel.)


 Blueprints are now more readily available in end-game missions if they were missed earlier on in the campaign.


Thanks again for taking the time to play Badlands Crew and make sure to let us know how you get on with the new patch over on Discord.

Curve Games & Runner Duck.

 Fixed an issue where there were duplicated defence towers in the conflagration outpost.

Curve Games & Runner Duck.

notes.title: Development Update – Enemy Faction Spotlight: The Gun Nutz
notes.notes:
Hello, Dave from Runner Duck here! I wanted to complete our series of posts about the enemy factions you’ll face in Badlands Crew with a look at ‘The Gun Nutz’…

To the South East of the starting area of Home Plateau lies the red eroded desert of the Lower Badlands, where you’ll run into The Gun Nutz patrolling its valleys and canyons.

The Gun Nutz are descendants of a community of preppers who sprung into action as society crumbled,
gleefully raiding army equipment storage sites, claiming the vast majority of conventional firearms and military vehicles in the land.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/6b96d8183a6651ed46f5157e6b82c88a0e5bafff.jpgA heavily armed Gun Nutz patrol harassing an ambushed Battle Wagon

Their commander in chief is the ruthless disciplinarian, Major Krank; as brutal to his own subordinates as he is to his enemies. Rumours abound that during his raids on military storage sites, he stumbled upon the last viable nuclear warhead in existence, which he wields to cow any potential challengers into submission.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/c22ac2c608fa2bd63d6c38e7d8fd55bcedbb1717.jpgEarly Concept Art for the Gun Nutz Faction’s Warlord (Major Krank), Symbol and crew characters

As for vehicles, The Gun Nutz bring to bear a range of military rides including jeeps, hummers, MRAPs, pickups and half tracks. With their ready-made fleet of piercing and blast damage resistant war machines, it’s wise to prepare carefully before confronting their patrols! Perhaps try ‘turning up the heat’ on them ;).

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/8b0f176f2e343c9fcaa6a97d19b5a15cb49d0f56.jpgThe Gun Nutz’ fleet of military vehicles in our ‘Virtual Parking Lot’.

The Gun Nutz’ armoury comprises a range of lethal conventional weapons, including machine guns, rifles, shotguns and grenade launchers. They have guns that are effective from close to long range, so keep those heads on a swivel!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/44ac4a228078bd88558e940ace5f9b81ba3c410b.pngL-R: A good ol’ 50 cal, a water-cooled electric drive ‘Scattermaster’ auto shotgun, ‘Doomster’ sawn off shotgun

Time for me to get back to the finishing touches on the project; it's been a long road, but now we’re just one week from release!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2078230/Badlands_Crew/

Thanks for reading!
Dave

notes.title: Development Update – Enemy Faction Spotlight: The Klowns
notes.notes:
Hi! Jon from Runner Duck here, sharing a quick look at another of the enemy factions in Badlands Crew - ‘The Klowns’.

To the East of the Lower Badlands, in the glistening whiteness of the Dessicated Salt Flats, is where you’re most likely to first encounter the Klowns faction. Devoid of shame, the Klowns intentionally appear ridiculous in order to obfuscate their true ruthless nature.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/6630fa11769c9cc1b170e2c7428592ba77067748.jpg
A Klowns “Ice Screamer” and “Re-Educator” terrorising the Salt Flats

The Klowns are ruled by “Giggles the Klown”, their psychopathic leader in greasepaint and a clown wig. Many of his followers who initially fell for his charming, harmless facade wish to escape from his faction, but the consequences for those captured are severe. They also hold territory around the edges of The Atomic City, and further to the East in Krazed Quarry.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/b09d0232b531375c68b3485da5ec1ee7aee8f597.jpg
Early Concept Art for the Klown Faction’s Warlord, Symbol and crew characters

The Klown’s fleet of vehicles feature some unusual choices, matching their origins as a chaotic circus troupe; their brightly coloured food trucks, school buses and even dodgems may look comical, but are bristling with weapons and pack a punch!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/9a9769980353dc7315b68a79b3b298f019dfa1da.jpg
Klown vehicles in our ‘Virtual Parking Lot’ scene, where we assemble the many variations

The Klowns primarily use two types of weaponry: toxic gas weapons which can inflict poison damage, and makeshift pneumatic cannons, firing golf balls or even bowling balls, which deal blunt damage and can cause crew to become stunned. Having spent too much time fooling around with their own toxic weapon supplies they are somewhat immune to toxic damage, so you’re better off using other weapon types against them!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/7ee917205dd728fcf31f1e6339fa1c6c41642d9c.png
L-R: ‘The Stinger’ BB gun, ‘Toxic Balloon Launcher’, ‘Screaming Splitter’ Bowling Ball Cannon

I hope you have the last laugh when you go up against Giggles in the Badlands!

That’s all for now, we’ve got to finish the game, because it’s out soon!
Jon

notes.title: Minor Demo Update
notes.notes:
Hello!

Just a very quick post to say thank you to everyone who downloaded and played the Badlands Crew demo. The response has been really positive for us, giving us a much needed boost as we embark on the final stretch of development.

An additional thank you to everyone who has left feedback for us; it's incredibly helpful and we appreciate you taking the time to let us know your thoughts and ideas! We do read all of it, but I hope you can forgive us for not responding to everyone, as we’re a small team of 4 and are now totally focused on making the game as good as it can be.

We’ve already made some changes based on your feedback, and a few of them were suitable to be included in a small update to the demo. Here’s a list of some of them courtesy of Jon:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/3f1995696bf37cfe1116866d01a310d076045b6a.jpg

Combat with boarding enemies has been adjusted. Nearby idle crewmates will automatically attack them.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/90fdf414e6326fbc6623782271e28d6da3adf70a.jpg

Crew are shown in their default stations in the Garage while building your vehicle.
You can assign crew to specific stations when selecting a station in the Garage.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/7045063dd2f919c4f7ddd6cd623191671db121f9.jpg

 Access space requirements for stations and utilities have been changed to be slightly less strict, allowing better placement of stations, weapons and utilities. In the example above, the Command Station is placed on the top of a stack of structure blocks with no additional space around it; this is now valid!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/9f4da003a75415002ce29b628a87f0a4599672df.jpg

 Added Battle Wagon Showcase to the main menu, where you can see a selection of Battle Wagons built by other players for some inspiration!

As I said, these are not the only changes we’ve made, just the ones that are suitable to include in a minor demo update. We do not expect to make any more updates to the demo, as we now are 100% working on finishing the main game.

Some players have commented on the difficulty of the demo, and they’re quite right - In order to show you enough of the full Badlands Crew experience, the missions in the demo are set part-way through the campaign. There’s so many aspects to learn about, such as the combat mechanics, crew skills/perks, and constructing your Battle Wagon from the ground up (to name a few), that there’s just not enough space to explain everything in a few missions!

Thanks again for all your attention, support and encouragement!

Dave

notes.title: Development Update – Enemy Faction Spotlight: The Vultures
notes.notes:
Hello!
Dave from Runner Duck here - I wanted to make some quick posts to share some details about the enemy factions you’ll face on the road in Badlands Crew. This time, ‘The Vultures’.

Badlands Crew is set in a future after the world has suffered a perfect storm of global catastrophes, leaving civilisation, culture and technology almost completely wiped clean. Humanity's survivors are left fractured and in disarray. In the vacuum of order the very worst of humanity rose to seize positions of power, preying on the people’s fear. The most ruthless and twisted became the fearsome Warlords, who terrorise the Badlands from their fortified Outposts and Strongholds.

Eventually, almost every survivor ended up captive in one of the Warlords’ gulag-like Strongholds; forced to scavenge and serve.Those who readily gave in to their greed and hatred were promoted by the Warlords to be their road warriors, irredeemably devoted to chaos and war.

If you stray into the more mountainous regions of the Badlands, you’ll be met by The Vultures, a faction that patrols the slopes, looking for the weak and vulnerable to swoop on and pick clean.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/45b0b20f8b101aa50b14d3f267dfd06062b75f10.pngA Vulture Patrol scours the moon-lit mountainside for easy pickings

The Vultures are commanded by Lord Griffon - a deeply greedy man who keeps tight control of food production in his Strongholds, gorging himself and leaving only scraps to be distributed among his many subjects.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/8a94de8e0437611ac2fd4ff8043f1a51417a8cc5.jpgEarly Concept Art for the Vulture Faction’s Warlord, Symbol and crew characters

We wanted to give each faction a distinct flavour, so decided to limit the era of vehicle they use to a single decade. In the case of The Vultures, they favour cars and trucks from the 1950s.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/01e6187ca06827f07744f3eb97466a8b0048feda.pngA selection of Vulture Vehicles, tooled up with Scrap Cannons and Blade Launchers

When it came to the Vulture’s armaments, we designed sets of blade launchers and scrap cannons. It seemed fitting that this faction would employ weapons that slash and tear.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/e794bb6f1be49da7e6f47301bddc8ddbe020b80f.pngL-R: A makeshift blade launcher constructed of a tin can and angle-grinder; A dual repeating scrap cannon, made from a pair of oil cans and a spring-loaded reloading mechanism; A Legendary multi-blade launcher, powered by a hefty electric motor.

I hope this brief glimpse begins to give a sense of the world we’ve been creating. I’ll continue to share more when I get a chance as we finish up the game!

Cheers!
Dave

notes.title: Development Update – Enemy Faction Spotlight: The Pyros
notes.notes:
Hi! Dave from Runner Duck here again to share a quick tidbit on one of the enemy factions in Badlands Crew - ‘The Pyros’.

As you make your way through the Badlands, you’ll need to capture enemy outposts and strongholds along the way, to extend your reach across the wastes. In order to do this, you must vanquish the forces of the Warlords that hold them. Each faction employs different weapon types, which can be crafted and installed on your own Battle Wagon once their blueprints have been found!

Beyond the mountainous region ruled by Lord Griffon’s Vultures, you’ll come across regions of smoke and fumes, territories held by The Pyros.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/0be74185a1eac07b6c6958ab71c5a0bb371e41c4.pngA Pyro Heavy Gunship patrols the Lava Flows

Commanded by Chief Dante, they believe that there is nothing left of worth in the world - the only path forward is to cleanse everything with flame, and enjoy watching it burn.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/31b92a4be597695313bdf3a0f450cac14cf7005b.jpgEarly Concept Art for the Pyro Faction’s Warlord, Symbol and crew characters

When it comes to vehicles, the Pyro’s decade of choice is the 1930s. In addition to huge, heavy old firetrucks, they have fleets of Ratrods, cut down to the basics and used as agile assault units.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/395214cac158c51932333bb353eaf2976322b235.pngPyro vehicles in our ‘Virtual Parking Lot’ scene, where we assemble the many variations

Of course, the Pyros are armed to the teeth with incendiary weapons. These vary from close-range flamers, to longer-range flame lances and fireball cannons.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/7599864720692dfd9a4b5bc6526e4315e3f5dc3c.pngL-R: A makeshift flamer cobbled together from an aerosol can and lighter; A dual fireball launcher made from old water bottles; A fearsome high-octane, wide-spread acetylene torch

That’s all for now, plenty of work still to do!
Catch you next time!
Dave

notes.title: Development Update – "The Wingnuts"
notes.notes:
Hello! I’m Jon from Runner Duck, and I’m writing the Development Update this time.

The Citadel is the main base of the player’s faction, a sanctuary, relatively safe from the dangers of the Badlands around it. The player will spend a fair amount of time in the Citadel, equipping their crew and building their vehicle, so it was important to us to make it a vibrant, lively and interesting place. Missions out in the Badlands can be brutal and tense, so allowing the player to return to an oasis of relative comfort and humanity between missions is important for balance. With these things in mind, we came up with the idea of the Citadel Band, “The Wingnuts”.

[previewyoutube=kIsg0JwXdhY;full][/previewyoutube]
Unlike the rock soundtrack of the missions, The Wingnuts play cheerful folk and skiffle influenced music. I reached out to a musician I knew in Brighton, who performs with a number of bands in a range of styles, who I thought would be perfect for this soundtrack. He wrote the songs, and put together a small group to perform and record them. The songs were so good that we soon realised we would have to step up our presentation of the band within the game in order to do them justice!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/fb031db467dde899e56e25201901a090d3936e02.pngThe real life musicians behind “The Wingnuts”

I have always found that when there are musicians animated in a game (or cartoon), it really adds to the sense of immersion if their animation closely matches the music they are actually playing. We were using a MIDI data import system to drive the drumming animation of crewmates in War Drums stations, so I extended this system to allow us to animate The Wingnuts.

MIDI DATA TRACKS
All of the music for The Wingnuts was performed live, so it did not have any pre-existing MIDI data to work from. - however, it was recorded along to a click track, so it is not too tricky for me to create ‘silent MIDI tracks’ which mimic what is being played by the actual musicians. For this, I use Ableton Live:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/01b44946f1564e3bfaea4129b619ea4a969a3a92.png‘Silent’ MIDI tracks matched to live performance audio in Ableton Live

One MIDI track is created per instrument. The guitar MIDI track is the most complex, as it has both the pitch of the note (which affects the fretboard hand’s position) and has midi notes which trigger different animations for picking up, picking down, big strums up, and big strums down. There is an additional MIDI track for voice and harmonica, which animates the band’s mouths. I create these tracks by ear, listening to the song and adding notes as appropriate. Authoring a full set of silent MIDI data for a track generally takes me around an hour.

Once finished, I save out the .mid files, and our code in Unity converts them into a list of animation events.

CHARACTER ANIMATION
Characters were first given base ‘groove’ animation loops, making them nod and bob along with the music - we take the beats per minute of the current track and use this to modify the speed of this animation so they all stay in time with the music.

To make the characters appear to be playing the correct pitch on their instruments, we created a set of animations in which their ‘fretting’ hands were placed at a certain position to play a certain pitch; we took these sets of pitch animations and assigned them to a Blend Tree; a feature of game engine animation systems which allows us to blend their motion together using a simple value input from the pitch tracks of the MIDI data.

We then layer animations for the instrument playing/plucking hands on top of this, along with some incidental variations of the base ‘groove’ animations and there we have it - fully animated musicians!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/d6132ba6ed0e0355b125536b591fb1ba7be9c20c.gifAdjusting the bass player’s ‘pitch’ blend tree live in the editor

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/41fb7b74cd513440c6411f16b7bfeb583f02ab0c.pngThe animation state machine for the guitarist’s strumming arm

FINISHING TOUCHES...
There are some other elements, outside of the animation which we had to consider. The band is placed on stage in the Citadel, so to sound natural, the music should sound as if it is coming from there. However, it can quickly become annoying if the music is only coming from one side while you are working on your vehicle (especially with headphones)! To address this, we use a dynamic spatial blend. When the camera moves or changes, we begin to blend towards the music being spatialised (so the position and direction of the band is taken into account). After a short while of the camera being in a new location, we blend away from the music being spatialised, to just being a standard stereo stream. We also combine this with some reverb and filtering, so that when the camera is far from the band, the music is less clear and contains the natural reverb you would expect from the cavernous space between the walls of the Citadel.

We’ve been listening to The Wingnuts play on in the background of the Citadel as we work developing the game; despite hearing the same set of tracks for hundreds if not thousands of hours, we haven’t got sick of it at all - in fact we find ourselves whistling the tunes when going about our lives outside of work! Testament to what an incredible job the real musicians did when writing and recording the music!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/822828ed0f5a985d84f23d6dcc3380970dd6aef3.pngA soothing bedtime ballad

Thanks for reading this far. I hope you enjoyed this small insight into our game!
Jon

notes.title: Development Update – The World of the Badlands
notes.notes:
Hello! Dave from Runner Duck here.

It’s been a while since I posted anything here, so it felt like time to give you all a quick update!
Since releasing Bomber Crew, Runner Duck has doubled in size - there’s now 4 of us!

Badlands Crew is by far our most ambitious project yet, the scale of the world being one of the main challenges for our little team.

I wanted to share a glimpse of one of the first of the 12 regions that will confront you in the game – The Lower Badlands. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/ef87fb332a024b926ffe2ca0bff17c0dedefcc73.png 
Captain Ironside Briefs a Crew on their next task in defense of the Citadel

This region is a dusty, eroded desert, scored with deep canyons that you’ll need to traverse to reach the stronghold of the reigning Warlord, Major Krank. His faction, the Gun Nutz, will be patrolling the rust coloured sands with their arsenal of salvaged military vehicles and firearms, ready to reduce your Battle Wagon to scrap.

Your Battle Wagon’s fuel tanks are not bottomless, so good navigation is key, as the region is prone to sandstorms that will make it harder to keep your bearings!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/13ae624b8d902911306f077c6ac9d5d188a2ec39.png
A Battle Wagon rumbles down towards the Lower Badlands from Home Plateau

The size of this one region is around 50 square km, and the entire world covers approximately 722 square km!

One challenge of building a world so large is generating navigation data for the player and enemy drivers to be able to negotiate their way around and plan routes efficiently. Jon solved this by creating a solution that looks at the various colliders in the world and bakes out a grid that the driver behaviors can use to quickly look up where the accessible areas are. Where more definition is required, each grid square will divide itself into 4 smaller squares. This structure is known as a Quadtree.

Every time a change is made to the layout of the world, the entire quadtree must be re-baked, which takes around 1 hour 15 minutes and results in about 350mb of navigation data on disk; We have a process running on a spare PC that automates this - minimising the disruption to our workflow.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/74b31d1e23eaf375d9397b178f695c64062cbd90.png
Editor view of the baked Quadtree Navigation data

When creating the world, I first block out the driveable surfaces using Unity’s Terrain tools, quickly defining the elevations, slopes and obstacle rock outcrops. Once that’s done, we can place spawners for enemy units, and start testing out missions in that area. When we’re happy with the layout, I do a pass of placing rock geometry to get the landscape looking the part. After that, it's a case of iterating and adding various smaller details, like ruined structures, cacti, destructible rock piles etc…

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/77ea7c3e43cc1e7f30f0c153ea02edbfb9274d2e.gif
Before and after lining the driveable areas of the region with rock geometry

We have a global day/night system that includes fog effects which can be overridden to set the right mood for each region. Below is a shot I took of the Lower Badlands at sunrise, during which a wild Sandworm just happened to make a surprise appearance - clever girl!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44301076/570278cb8ac54d5d14523ad6156c339d6b7b57d1.gif
Sunrise over Calamity Canyon in the Lower Badlands towards Smokestack Stronghold

If you’re interested in posts that are a bit more techy and dev insight focused, please let us know - we’ll try to do some more when we get a spare moment.

OK, I’ve got to get back to the project now - thanks for reading!

Dave
Runner Duck

notes.title: Summer Development Update
notes.notes:
Hi Crewmates!

Sharing the latest Badlands news and a development update for you from Runner Duck towers.
Firstly, we’re taking part in the upcoming Tiny Teams event on Steam! This is a massive opportunity for a small team like us, to be featured alongside some of the best indie devs out there. We're thrilled that all the hard work that we’re putting into Badlands Crew has been recognised by the Yogscast. Make sure you check out the Yogscast’s streams, you might catch some Badlands Crew gameplay among some other fantastic games made by some great Tiny Teams!

Badlands Crew is our most ambitious project ever. At this point, there’s thousands of different ways to customise both your crew and your wagon. We’re going to go out on a limb and say that Badlands Crew will be our most rewarding game to date – we’ve been working hard to make sure that you will have a deeper and more involved experience of progression throughout your playthrough, more than any other Crew game.

At the beginning of Badlands Crew, your gunners will start out with your trusty Junk Lobber (it gets the job done), but by the end of Badlands Crew, you’ll have engaged in battles employing flamethrowers, buzz saw railguns, toxic gas launchers and more.
You’ll also see your wagon evolve over time, starting off as a rudimentary single-trailer rig before you unlock larger trailers and the option to attach up to three trailers to your wagon. Over time, you’ll build a customisable behemoth that will leave the Warlords of the Badlands quaking in their boots.
Badlands Crew also has a wide variety of missions for you to complete. Whether you're racing against the elusive nomad, 'Gekko’, clearing areas of marauding enemy war bands, rescuing captive survivors, stomping out juvenile sandworms (and running from bigger adults!) or capturing outposts and strongholds – The Badlands will keep you on your toes.
That’s all before we get into our all new stat and perk system, which will open up endless possibilities to fine tune your crew builds.

We can’t wait for you to get your hands on Badlands Crew. As a small team of four, delivering new features, systems, tech and content at this scale means that we need to take the necessary time to deliver you the best game we can make, and so we will now be releasing Badlands Crew in 2025.

Thank you for all of the support that you have given us over the years, it means the world to us.
We’ll have more updates to share with you soon!
Sincerely,

Dave, Greg, Joe, and Jon
The Runner Duck Team.
